tasks.name: write a small CLI from a spec
tasks.prompt: Write {T}/minicount.py, a command line tool (python3 standard library only). Usage: python3 minicount.py [-l] [-w] [-c] [--longest] [FILE ...]. It counts lines (number of newline characters), words (whitespace separated), characters (decoded as UTF-8, not bytes) and the length in characters of the longest line (without its newline). Flags choose which counts are printed; with no flag it prints lines, words and characters. The order is ALWAYS lines, words, characters, longest, whatever the flag order. One output line per file: the selected counts separated by single spaces, then a space and the file name, e.g. `4 6 29 11 a.txt`. With two or more readable files print a final line with the sums (longest = the maximum) and the name `total`. With no FILE (or the name -) read standard input and show the name - . A file that cannot be opened prints `minicount: NAME: No such file` to standard error, is skipped (not in the total), and makes the exit code 1 at the end. Sample input files are in {T}/samples.

tasks.name: make a migration survive bad rows
tasks.prompt: {T}/migrate.py converts a csv: python3 migrate.py IN OUT REJECTS. On {T}/orders_in.csv it crashes. Change migrate.py so that it never crashes on a bad row: good rows go to OUT exactly as now (price_cents = price in euros times 100, rounded to a whole number), and each bad row goes to REJECTS, a csv with header id,name,qty,price,reason holding the ORIGINAL four values and a reason. A row is bad when: id is not an integer (reason bad_id), else name is empty after trimming (empty_name), else qty is not an integer (bad_qty), else price is not a number (bad_price). Row order is kept in both files. Exit code 0. Run it on orders_in.csv to produce {T}/out.csv and {T}/rejects.csv. It will also be run on another input file.

tasks.name: join two csv files with rules

tasks.name: convert ini to typed json with interpolation
tasks.prompt: Write {T}/ini2json.py (python3 standard library; usage: python3 ini2json.py IN.ini OUT.json) converting an ini file to JSON, and run it on {T}/app.ini to produce {T}/app.json. Rules: each section becomes an object; blank lines and lines starting with ; or # are ignored; a value that is an integer (optional minus sign, digits, NO leading zero unless it is exactly 0) becomes a JSON integer; a decimal like 0.75 or -0.5 becomes a float; yes/true/on and no/false/off in any letter case become true/false; keys whose name ends in _list become a list of trimmed strings (empty items dropped); everything else stays a string (so 02134 stays a string); ${section.key} inside a value is replaced by that other value (which may itself contain references). It will be run on other ini files too.
